- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (≥15% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation; add 3–5% to forecast for momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days relative to sentiment shift.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 2–4% per day until convergence with true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is negative or flat, model tends to overpredict recovery; reduce forecast by 5–8% to align with sentiment-driven caution.
